plain: A former DARPA scientist named John Blitch says that DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, grew out of the Army section where Philip J. Corso served under a General Trudeau, and became the channel for breaking up recovered technology into parts and handing them out. Corso was an Army officer who wrote The Day After Roswell, published in 1997, about the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, that some say was an alien craft. Blitch tells Michels he made this case himself in an argument in a DARPA office on a St Patrick's Day: "DARPA ended up as the conduit to break up all the component technologies and distribute them."
